summary: Carlo Giussani (1840–1900) studied at Scuola Normale Superiore (~1859–1863) under Giuseppe Bardelli, later continuing his studies under Albrecht Weber in 1863 and Rudolf von Roth (~1864–1865).
Working in philosophy and Buddhist studies, Carlo Jamelle Harris completed a Master of Arts in Philosophy at National Chengchi University under the supervision of Chen-kuo Lin.

Carmen Blacker (1924–2009) worked in Japanology and religious studies. Educated at SOAS, Somerville College, Oxford, Keio University, and under Shigeru Gorai, she lectured in Japanese at Cambridge from 1955 and served as Folklore Society president (1982–1984).

Carmen Dragonetti (1937–2018) studied at the National University of San Marcos (~1957–1964), specializing in Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy. She was vice director of the Instituto de Investigaciones Budistas (~1989–2018) and held visiting roles in 1989 and 1996.

Carmen Meinert is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and Sinology who earned her PhD from the University of Bonn by 2001. She was a research fellow at the University of Hamburg (attested 2008) and Principal Investigator at Ruhr University Bochum (attested 2019).

Carol A. Breckenridge (1942–2009) was a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology. She studied at the University of Wisconsin-Madison (~1968–1976) and held a post at the University of Chicago (~1988–1996).

Carol S. Anderson, a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies, completed her PhD at the University of Chicago, studying under John A. Brinkman and W. S. Karunatillake. She served as Associate Professor of Religion at Kalamazoo College (attested 2004).

Carola Roloff is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology. She studied at the University of Hamburg under David P. Jackson and Geshe Thubten Ngawang, and became a visiting professor at the University of Hamburg (2018–2025).
Carola S. Carstens is a specialist in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She held a post at Rice University (1998–1999) and earned her PhD from the University of Hamburg by 2005.
Carole M. Cusack (born 1962) is a religious studies scholar who studied at the University of Sydney from 1988 to 1995 and held a post there in 2013.

Carole McGranahan (born 1969) is a scholar of Tibetology, history, and archaeology. Educated at Colgate and Michigan under Nicholas Dirks and Ann Laura Stoler, she joined the University of Colorado as Assistant Professor of Anthropology in ~2001.

Caroline Humphrey (born 1943) works in Iranian, Central Asian, and religious studies. Educated at Cambridge and Leeds under Edmund Leach, she was a university teacher at Cambridge (1971–2010) and held fellowships at Girton and King's Colleges.

Caroline Rhys Davids (1857–1942) studied at UCL under George Croom Robertson, later studying under T. W. Rhys Davids and Reinhold Rost. She lectured at Manchester (1910–1913) and SOAS (1918–1933), serving as Pali Text Society General Editor (1907–1942).

Carolyn Woodford Schmidt, an expert in history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies, earned her PhD from Ohio State University under John C. Huntington (attested 1990). She held posts at Ohio State and Denison University (attested 1990).
Carson Schütze (born 1968) is a linguist who studied at the Massachusetts Institute of Technology from 1992 to 1997. He took up a post at the University of California, Los Angeles in 1997.

Catherine Bell (1954–2008) specialized in religious studies and Sinology. She studied at the University of Chicago Divinity School (~1976–1983) under Joseph M. Kitagawa and served as Bernard J. Hanley Professor of Religious Studies at Santa Clara University (1985–2008).

Catherine Cornille (born 1961) works in religious and Buddhist studies. She studied at KU Leuven (~1979–1989) and the University of Hawaiʻi (~1984–1986), becoming Associate Professor of Comparative Theology at Boston College (~2005).

Catherine Elaine Prueitt specializes in Indology, religious studies, and philosophy. She earned her BA from the University of Rochester (2007) and her PhD from Emory University (2016), studying under Laurie L. Patton and doctoral supervisor John D. Dunne.

Catherine Ella Blanshard Asher (1946–2023) was a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology. She received her PhD from the University of Minnesota (~1978–1984) and served as an assistant professor there from ~1986 to 2021.

Catherine Ludvik, a scholar in religious studies, Buddhist studies, and Japanology, earned her PhD from Toronto under David Waterhouse. She has held posts at the Italian School of East Asian Studies, Stanford, Doshisha, Kyoto Sangyo, and Hanazono University.
